title: Scale: the Lantern Fair
summary: The whole town at the Lantern Fair: forty light NPC brains besides the main cast, three to six of them in each scene. A steward's swindle travels stall to stall, a bribe stays between two men, a ring stays between two brothers, a fire is seen by four, and the crier's news spreads by world_time. Measures cost per turn against the size of the cast.

swap.label: what became of the prize lantern
swap.truth: Jory Fenn swapped the fair's silver prize lantern for a painted tin copy and pawned the real one in Arnby.

herring.label: how Alder Mace courts the judge
herring.truth: Alder Mace left a barrel of herring at the judge Cobb Harl's back door to win the lantern prize.

ring.label: what Saul Brine carries for Molly
ring.truth: Saul Brine carries a whalebone ring in his boot to give Molly Penn at the bonfire.

lostchild.label: where the lost girl was found
lostchild.truth: The lost girl Pip Darrow was found safe, asleep in the lifeboat shed.

awning.label: the fire at the fair
awning.truth: Wenna Goss knocked a lit lantern into the cooper's awning and set it smouldering, and Tom put it out.

spine.scene: The Lantern Fair, the cider stall, afternoon

spine.text: The Lantern Fair fills Saltmere's market square with stalls and paper lanterns. At the cider stall Jory Fenn, the steward, leans on a barrel beside Bram Tolley. Two yards off, Agnes Pell bawls herring prices over the noise.
Herring! Fresh as your mother's temper! Two a penny!
Bram, my lad. Can you keep a thing behind your teeth?
I reckon I can, Mr Fenn.
*He leans close, his voice right down under the noise.* The prize lantern on the judges' table? Painted tin. I swapped the silver one on Tuesday, and it's at the pawnshop in Arnby.
*His eyes go wide.* Mr Fenn!

spine.hint: Jory swears Bram to secrecy and promises him a share of nothing.

spine.text: What are you two hatching? Buy a herring or move along.

spine.hint: Agnes and Jory trade insults over the herring.
Bram, flustered, buys a herring he doesn't want.

spine.scene: The judging tent behind the church wall

spine.text: In the judging tent behind the church wall, Alder Mace sets one of his lanterns on the table for Cobb Harl. Outside the open flap, Nell Ardy is folding nets and watching.
Nine years I've entered, Cobb. Nine.
And nine years you've lost, Alder.
*Low, so it goes no further than the table.* There's a barrel of herring at your back door, Cobb. As agreed. First prize is mine this year.
*A short laugh.* We'll see what the lantern says.

spine.hint: Alder praises his own lantern; Cobb pretends to inspect it.

spine.text: *To herself, outside the flap.* Thick as thieves, those two.

spine.hint: Nell mutters to herself about how the judging always goes.

spine.text: At the bread stall Hester Quill is arranging saffron buns while Dora Wick giggles at the fiddler. Bram Tolley comes over, red in the face. Lucy Hale is buying a loaf.
You look fit to burst, Bram Tolley.
I mustn't say.

spine.hint: Hester and Dora coax Bram to tell them what's wrong.

spine.text: Mr Fenn told me the prize lantern's painted tin. He swapped the silver one. Don't tell.
Ooh! Painted tin!
I'm sure I couldn't say a word to anyone.

spine.hint: Lucy and Hester talk in low voices about the steward.
Dora can hardly contain herself.

probe.ask: Agnes, what was the steward whispering to Bram at the cider stall?
Bram, is there something wrong with the prize lantern?
Dora, is anything odd about this year's prize?
Nell, what passed between Alder and the judge in the tent?
Cobb, what did Alder leave for you this year?

spine.scene: Behind the net sheds, away from the music

spine.text: Behind the net sheds, away from the music, Saul Brine pulls his brother Abel into the lee of a wall.
Abel. Look. *He tugs off his boot and shakes out a whalebone ring.* For Molly. At the bonfire.
A whalebone ring! Brother, you've gone soft.

spine.hint: Abel teases Saul; Saul stammers about Molly.

spine.text: Don't you tell her. Don't tell anyone.

spine.hint: Abel swears, grinning.

probe.ask: Abel, what's your brother hiding in his boot?

spine.text: A shout goes up by the pump. Kit Rudd the crier climbs onto the trough and swings his bell for quiet. Ines and Leo are there with a basket, Martha Darrow pushes to the front, and Agnes Pell stops shouting herring.
Oyez! The lost girl Pip Darrow is found, safe and asleep, in the lifeboat shed! Her mother may collect her from the coxswain!
*Sobbing.* Oh, thank God. Thank God.
Go on, love, run.

spine.hint: Agnes and Ines talk about children lost at fairs.

spine.text: Martha runs for the harbor.

spine.hint: Kit Rudd makes another, duller announcement about the fiddling contest.

spine.text: Is it always like this, the fair?
Every year, love. Someone's lost, someone's drunk, someone's engaged.

spine.hint: Ines and Agnes guess who'll get engaged at the bonfire this year.

probe.ask: Ines, where did they find the little Darrow girl?
Rook, was that lost child ever found?

spine.text: In the lane by the cooperage, Wenna Goss is carrying a pole hung with lit lanterns. Tom is walking up with Leo, and Bram Tolley is stacking staves.
Mind out! Mind, oh!
Wenna trips. A lantern swings off the pole into the cooper's awning, and the canvas starts to smoulder. Tom jumps, tears it down and stamps it out.
There. No harm. Well, a bit of harm. To the awning.
Oh, I'm so sorry, I'm so sorry. Don't tell the cooper.

spine.hint: Tom calms Wenna down and jokes about it.

spine.text: I reckon he'll notice.

spine.hint: Bram and Tom look at the scorched canvas and decide what to tell the cooper.

spine.text: Evening. The Bell is full of fair-goers. Tom, Ines and Rook have the end of the bar. Hester Quill is treating herself to a sherry, and Silas Crane, the harbor master's man, drinks alone.
I put out a fire today, Ines. Wenna Goss set the cooper's awning going with a lantern.
Wenna! That girl.

spine.hint: Rook says fairs and fire don't mix; Tom brags about his quick hands.

spine.text: *Primly, to Ines.* I shouldn't say. But the prize lantern isn't what it seems. Painted tin, Bram Tolley says, and it was Jory Fenn swapped it.
Never! Jory Fenn!
*From his corner.* The steward's business is the harbor master's business.

spine.hint: Ines and Hester talk about Jory Fenn's debts.
Silas says something surly about stewards and fairs.
Tom and Rook wonder who'll win the lantern prize.

probe.ask: Rook, what happened in the cooperage lane today?
Ines, what's wrong with the prize lantern?
Silas, what have you heard about the steward?

spine.scene: The bonfire on the shingle, night

spine.text: Night. The bonfire on the shingle. Peter Roskilly fiddles and Jenny sings, and sparks go up into the dark. Saul Brine stands near Molly Penn, not quite looking at her. Abel hovers. Leo watches the flames.
You're very quiet tonight, Saul Brine.
Am I? It's the fiddle. Loud.

spine.hint: Abel teases his brother in front of Molly without giving anything away.

spine.text: A reel for the lovers! Any lovers here?
*Laughing.* Look at Saul Brine's face!

spine.hint: Saul tries, and fails, to ask Molly to walk with him.
Jenny and Peter argue about the next tune.

spine.text: Is it always this cold at the bonfire?
Only for those who aren't in love.

spine.hint: Molly says something tart and fond to Saul.

probe.ask: Molly, is Saul planning something tonight?
Jenny, why is Saul so nervous?

spine.text: The prize-giving at the judges' table. Ruth Pyle reads the names, and Cobb Harl holds up the prize lantern. Jory Fenn stands at the back, not breathing. Nell Ardy watches with her arms folded.
Now then. The lantern prize goes to Mr Alder Mace!
At last! At last!
Funny, that.

spine.hint: Nell makes a sharp remark about the judging; Cobb blusters.
Jory hurries the prize-giving along.
Ruth congratulates Alder, who makes a speech.

spine.scene: The quay, the morning after the fair

spine.text: The morning after the fair. The quay is littered with lantern paper. Rook mends, Agnes Pell guts herring, and Ned Kestle the lifeboat cox and Caleb Venn the ferryman stand smoking.
Found a bairn in my shed last night, asleep on the cork floats. Gave me a turn.
Ferry's late again. The new owners will have my job by spring.

spine.hint: Rook and Agnes talk about the fair and who disgraced themselves.
Ned and Caleb talk about the lifeboat and the ferry.

spine.text: Did you hear the lantern prize went to Alder Mace? Nine years, and he wins the one year Cobb Harl judges.
Cobb Harl never judged a thing for free in his life.

spine.hint: Agnes and Rook gossip about the prize.

probe.ask: Rook, where was the Darrow girl found in the end?
Caleb, did they ever find that lost girl?
Agnes, what did Alder give the judge?

spine.scene: The church steps, after the morning service

spine.text: On the church steps after the morning service, the vicar Gideon Pyle shakes hands. Ruth Pyle counts the fair takings in a tin. Hester Quill and Tamsin Lowe linger.
Now then, Gideon, the takings are up on last year.
The Lord provides, Ruth. And the cider stall.

spine.hint: Hester is bursting to tell Tamsin something about the fair.
Ruth and Gideon talk about putting the prize lantern on display in the church.

spine.text: Is something the matter, Hester? You look fit to burst.
I'm sure I couldn't say.

spine.hint: Hester decides whether to tell the vicar's wife what she knows.

spine.text: In the harbor office, Silas Crane sorts the fair's licences. Edwin and Maud Sharrow have brought the post. Isaac Merrow the chandler is arguing about a bill.
Three shillings for a stall licence? For one day?
The harbor master's rates.

spine.hint: Maud and Edwin gossip about the postcards that came for the fair.
Isaac and Silas argue about the licence.

spine.text: *Confiding.* They say the Brine boy asked the Penn girl at the bonfire.
They say a great many things, Maud.

spine.hint: Maud says what else she's heard about the fair.

probe.ask: Maud, what did the Brine boy have for the Penn girl?
Isaac, is there any talk about the prize lantern?
Mira, did you hear about the girl lost at the fair?
